Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual-signals skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence and inherited guidance before touching the controller. I’ll stay strictly within this Phase 2 workspace and the no-Bookshelf evidence boundary.

The wake-visual-signals skill applies here: it requires comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure, anchored by observations, metrics, diagnostics, and shared prewarm imagery. I’m using that evidence order before forming or editing the policy hypothesis.

The current finite winner is the 1700°/time² posterior-command ceiling: it preserves the same active turn-then-diagonal route and reaches 3.72 time units sooner with lower mean distance and effort. Its force/moment load increase is substantial, so I’m treating it as a navigation/effort tradeoff—not yet a clean all-metric improvement—and checking it against the inherited failed damping continuation before selecting the one follow-on probe.

The visual-evidence skill’s control diagnosis is now recorded before the policy edit. I’m selecting one isolated 1750°/time² posterior ceiling—the midpoint between the repeated 1800-envelope anchor and the 1700 tradeoff—to test whether the large navigation/effort gain can be retained with materially lower loads.

The candidate and reusable lesson are both updated. I’m now invoking the prescribed non-CFD checks separately: guidance semantic change, Julia policy contract/schema, then editable-boundary validation.

The first prescribed check found a duplicated “copied to guidance” marker in the rendered root README—both lines name the same assigned parent—so it cannot resolve a unique parent. I’m removing only that duplicate marker and rerunning the check; this does not alter solver behavior or guidance evidence.

The Julia contract check did not execute because `julia` is absent from the shell PATH (the policy itself did not fail). I’m checking the environment’s standard Julia locations, then I’ll rerun the exact contract command if a binary is available; the other prescribed checks continue independently.

Guidance validation and editable-boundary validation now pass. Julia is not installed in this environment, so I’m completing the deterministic schema/reference audit and file-diff review statically; I’ll report that environment limitation explicitly rather than claim the runtime check executed.
